facets.answer: NVIDIA reported shipping its first Vera Rubin samples to customers in February 2026, and management later said it was on track to begin production shipments in Q3 2026. Huang also said Vera Rubin was already in production, and a third-party report said volume production had started. These support sample shipments and reported production activity, but do not establish completed commercial-quantity shipments or their scale. Production-shipment timing remains forward-looking; supply-chain and geopolitical pressures are a reported risk, not evidence a delay occurred.

Customer interest and planned use are evident, including reported customer sign-ups for Vera CPUs, SK Telecom’s planned Vera Rubin AI factory for 2027, and SpaceX’s planned satellite payload. CoreWeave reported completing NVL72 bring-up and validation in June 2026, an actual technical-readiness milestone. But the supplied evidence does not establish an operating Vera Rubin customer deployment. Plans and sign-ups are not completed deployments; the SK partnership includes letters of intent that a cited report says are usually non-binding.

Vera-specific realized revenue is not established. NVIDIA’s nearly $20 billion figure is forward-looking CPU revenue guidance, and Huang clarified it refers to standalone CPU, not Vera Rubin systems. Third-party reporting also describes roughly $20 billion in expected Vera sales, but that remains a forecast. Revenue may also be difficult to verify separately without disclosure; the material provides no realized Vera-specific revenue result.
